title: Uniform truncation window for proper classical direct images after base change
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of schemes. Suppose $e\geq0$ bounds the dimensions of all fibres after every base change [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For any scheme map $S\to Y$, write $f_S:X_S=X\times_YS\to S$. In the ordinary constant-$A$ unbounded pro-étale derived categories, let $J\in D(X_S,A)$ have classical cohomology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. For integers $m,N$ with $N<m-2e-1$, the canonical truncation map induces a natural isomorphism of sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$
$$\mathcal H^mRf_{S,*}J\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^mRf_{S,*}\tau_{\geq N}J.$$
Use total K-injective direct image and good truncations [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] [def-kun-truncations]. The same $e$ and inequality work for every $S$.

source.place: Étale statements, both sides depend on a bounded-below truncation; old split steps 9–10

proof.text: Fix S and g and put p = pullback.snd f g. Properness survives base change and the assumed fibre bound gives dimension at most e for every fibre of p. For an étale module sheaf H over the finite ring ULift A, its underlying abelian sheaf is torsion. Apply the proper torsion cohomological-dimension bound and the module/abelian higher-direct-image comparison to obtain R^q p_* H = 0 for q > 2e. Faithfulness of the module forgetful functor reflects the zero object.

source.place: Étale statements: the uniform proper cohomological-dimension bound

proof.text: A classical fixed-coefficient pro-étale module sheaf is the comparison inverse image of an étale module sheaf. The canonical bounded-below direct-image comparison applied to that sheaf in degree zero, and exactness of comparison inverse image, transfer the bound q > 2e to its total pro-étale direct image. The canonical intrinsic realization has the same underlying set sheaf: its module-sheafification unit is already an isomorphism on the underlying abelian sheaf. Its counit and derived direct-image comparison therefore transport this heart bound to the intrinsic constant-ring modules of the statement.

source.place: Transfer: exact comparison and the constant-coefficient realization

proof.text: For a triangulated functor with heart bound 2e on classical sheaves, induct on the length of a finite cohomology interval [a,b]. An interval of length zero is a shift of its single cohomology sheaf; the empty interval is zero. The good-truncation triangle at b reduces the successor case to [a,b-1] and [b,b]. The truncation maps identify cohomology in the retained degrees, preserving classicality. The long cohomology sequence gives vanishing in degree r whenever b+2e < r.

source.place: Étale statements: dévissage by the bounded-below truncations

proof.text: Countable products are exact in the intrinsic pro-étale module categories. Total direct image preserves them because the exact inverse-image/direct-image adjunction induces an unbounded derived adjunction. Apply the finite-interval bound to every truncation tau_ge(-n) L of a classical complex L in degrees at most b. Left completeness and preservation of countable products give R p_* L in degrees at most b+2e+1, including when L is unbounded below.

source.place: Étale statements and Transfer: passage to unbounded complexes by left completeness

proof.text: Set L = tau_lt(N) J. Its cohomology is classical by the canonical truncation inclusion, and it lies in degrees at most N-1. The preceding bound places R p_* L in degrees at most N+2e. The assumed N < m-2e-1 makes its cohomology in degrees m and m+1 zero. The image under R p_* of the canonical good-truncation triangle L -> J -> tau_ge(N) J then shows that H^m of its second arrow is an isomorphism. This is exactly the map in the statement, without replacing it by an unspecified isomorphic map. The construction uses arbitrary S and the given uniform e.
